description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 2 of
t/op/universal.t.  PRE-EXISTING.  5 blessed rows.

`UNIVERSAL::VERSION` is the method every class inherits: with no argument it
returns the class's `$VERSION`; with one it COMPARES and dies if the class is
older.  t/op/universal.t lines 124-138:

    $Alice::VERSION = 2.718;
    cmp_ok eval { $a->VERSION }, '==', 2.718;          # perl 2.718   PCL undef
    eval { $a->VERSION(2.719) };
    like $@, qr/^Alice version 2.719 required--this is only version 2.718 at /;
                                                        # perl matches  PCL ''
    ok (eval { $a->VERSION(2.718) });                   # perl 1       PCL ''
    $Alice::VERSION = "2.7.18";
    eval { $a->VERSION(2.719) };
    like $@, qr/^Invalid version format/;               # perl matches  PCL ''
    eval { $a->VERSION("2.7.19") };
    like $@, qr/^Invalid version format/;               # perl matches  PCL ''

PCL answers undef for the no-argument form and never raises either diagnostic.

WHAT IS RELATED AND WHAT IS NOT: `use Foo 1.23` (the VERSION check at import
time) is a different site.  #1665 is perl's VERSION GRAMMAR (v-strings,
`package Foo v1.2.3`); this is the METHOD.  A fix should read `$VERSION`
through the same normalisation #1665 owns rather than inventing a second one.

ROWS: t/op/universal.t tests 84, 86, 87, 90, 92 (the rowkeys are the unnamed
`[at t/op/universal.t line 125|128|130|134|138]`).


=== CLOSED as a DUPLICATE of #1743, fixed s492c (2026-09-21) ===
Same stub, same fix; see #1743's DONE section.  Note for whoever reads the
five t/op/universal.t rows quoted here: perl 5.40.3 does NOT answer
"Invalid version format" to the two rows this task attributes it to --
`$VERSION = "2.7.18"; $a->VERSION(2.719)` dies with the ORDINARY "version
required" message, because version-object comparison finds v2.7.18 <
v2.719.0.  PCL matches perl 5.40.3, which is the oracle.
